WhiteHouse.title: Trump Effect: American Manufacturing Is Roaring Back as Factory Activity Hits Four-Year High
WhiteHouse.summary:
The White House press release reports that the U.S. manufacturing sector is experiencing growth for the third consecutive month, with key indexes such as the Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing index and the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia’s Manufacturing Index showing strong performance. Manufacturing job growth in the first quarter of 2026 was positive for the first time in three years.

Several major companies are making large investments in U.S. manufacturing:  
- Apple plans to invest $600 billion over four years, creating 20,000 jobs.  
- Nvidia is investing $500 billion to produce AI chips and infrastructure entirely in the U.S.  
- Johnson & Johnson, AstraZeneca, Bristol Myers Squibb, and GSK are investing billions in domestic manufacturing of pharmaceuticals.  
- GlobalFoundries is investing $16 billion in semiconductor manufacturing.  
- Stellantis is investing $13 billion to expand domestic production.

U.S. Steel is reopening its Gary Tin Mill in Indiana, creating 225 jobs, a facility that had closed in 2022. The reopening is attributed to tariff enforcement. Industry leaders attribute growth to factors including trade enforcement, onshoring of manufacturing, infrastructure funding, and supply chain regionalization.

The release includes quotes from CEOs of U.S. Steel, Steel Dynamics, Cleveland Cliffs, Nvidia, Apple, and Eli Lilly expressing support for current manufacturing trends and investments in the U.S.

Overall, the release states that U.S. manufacturing is expanding with significant investment, job creation, and reshoring of production under President Trump’s administration.

WhiteHouse.title: Nominations Sent to the Senate
WhiteHouse.summary:
The White House announced the following nominations sent to the Senate:

- Riley Barnes, of Texas, nominated as Director of the Peace Corps.
- Rudolph Bauer, of South Carolina, nominated as Ambassador to Belize.
- Don Richard Berthiaume, Jr., of Virginia, nominated as Inspector General of the Department of Justice.
- Sean Costello, of Alabama, nominated as United States Attorney for the Southern District of Alabama for a four-year term.
- Erich Hernandez-Baquero, of Florida, nominated as Assistant Secretary of the Air Force.
- Roger Mason, of Virginia, nominated as Director of the National Reconnaissance Office.
- Christopher Phelan, of Minnesota, nominated as Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers.
- Erica Schwartz, of Florida, nominated as Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
- Gary Shatswell, of Washington, nominated as Assistant Secretary of Veterans Affairs for Information and Technology.

WhiteHouse.title: President Trump Addresses Key Issues Facing the Nation in Exclusive CNBC Interview
WhiteHouse.summary:
President Donald J. Trump gave an interview on CNBC’s Squawk Box discussing several topics:

- He said the U.S. is in a strong negotiating position with Iran and expects a favorable deal, noting 47 years of past conflicts.
- Trump stated that a responsible agreement could benefit the Iranian people and help Iran become a legitimate nation.
- He indicated the U.S. is prepared to take military action if negotiations with Iran fail.
- Trump criticized House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other Democrats for comments he believes undermine U.S. negotiations.
- He warned that failing to address the Iranian threat could lead to severe consequences, including a negative impact on the stock market and security threats.
- Trump said NATO is not necessary for U.S. security, describing it as dependent on the U.S.
- He expressed support for his Federal Reserve nominee, Kevin Warsh.
- Trump commented on interest rates, supporting rate increases to curb inflation but advocating for the U.S. to have the lowest interest rates globally.
- He discussed problems in the airline industry, mentioning that Spirit Airlines is struggling and expressing opposition to its merger with other airlines.
- Trump criticized recent changes to college sports related to Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) policies and court rulings, saying they have harmed college sports programs.

The full interview is available for viewing.

WhiteHouse.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Issues Presidential Determination to Support U.S. Air Force Jet Fighter Training Operations
WhiteHouse.summary: President Donald J. Trump signed a Presidential Determination exempting U.S. Air Force jet fighter training operations in Idaho, Oregon, and Nevada from certain Clean Water Act regulations for one year, while maintaining compliance with other federal standards. The exemption aims to support military training critical to maintaining combat readiness. Additional actions mentioned include executive orders focused on modernizing defense acquisitions, updating medical standards, improving foreign defense sales, addressing defense contractor priorities, and ensuring reliable power supply for military facilities. The Department of Defense was also given a secondary historic title, "Department of War."

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Grid Infrastructure, Equipment, and Supply Chain Capacity
WhiteHouse.summary: The memorandum from the President to the Secretary of Energy declares that the United States’ electric grid infrastructure and its supply chains are critical to national defense. It states that the current capacity to design, produce, and deploy key grid components—such as transformers, transmission lines, substations, and related materials—is limited due to dependence on foreign sources, long production times, and insufficient domestic investment. The President determines that purchasing, financial support, and other actions under section 303 of the Defense Production Act are necessary and the most effective ways to address these issues. A national emergency was declared under Executive Order 14156, and certain legal requirements are waived to allow for rapid expansion of domestic grid infrastructure production. The Secretary of Energy is authorized to carry out this determination and to publish it in the Federal Register.

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Development, Manufacturing, and Deployment of Large-Scale Energy and Energy‑Related Infrastructure
WhiteHouse.summary:
On January 20, 2025, President Donald J. Trump declared a national energy emergency under Executive Order 14156, citing inadequate U.S. energy production, transportation, refining, and generation as threats to the nation's economy, security, and foreign policy.  

He determined that the development, manufacturing, and deployment of large-scale energy and energy-related infrastructure are essential to national defense but are hindered by financing risks, regulatory delays, and market barriers.  

Under section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, the President:  
1. Declared these energy-related industrial resources and technologies essential to national defense.  
2. Found that U.S. industry cannot provide these capabilities promptly without Presidential intervention.  
3. Stated that purchases, financial support, and related actions under the Act are the most efficient means to address these needs.  

He waived specific procedural requirements of the Act to enable expanding domestic capability in this area and authorized the Secretary of Energy to implement this determination, including making necessary purchases and financial commitments. This determination will be published in the Federal Register.

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Natural Gas Transmission, Processing, Storage, and Liquefied Natural Gas Capacity
WhiteHouse.summary: The President issued a memorandum under the Defense Production Act related to natural gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG) capacity. The memorandum references Executive Order 14156, which declared a national energy emergency due to foreign actors manipulating energy markets. The President determined that natural gas and LNG infrastructure—including pipelines, processing plants, storage, liquefaction, export facilities, and related distribution—is essential for national defense and allied energy security. The memorandum states that without presidential action, the U.S. industry cannot expand this capacity quickly enough because of financial, construction, permitting, and infrastructure challenges. Therefore, the President authorizes using special powers under the Defense Production Act to support and accelerate development of natural gas and LNG capacity. These powers include making purchases, financial commitments, and other actions. The memorandum directs the Secretary of Energy to implement this determination and publish it in the Federal Register.

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Coal Supply Chains and Baseload Power Generation Capacity
WhiteHouse.summary:
The President issued a memorandum to the Secretary of Energy regarding coal supply chains and baseload power generation capacity under the Defense Production Act of 1950. 

Key points:

- On January 20, 2025, Executive Order 14156 declared a national energy emergency, citing inadequate energy production, transportation, refining, and generation capacity as threats to the U.S. economy, national security, and foreign policy.
- Reliable coal supply chains and baseload power generation capacity are essential to national defense, providing critical stability to the power grid that supports defense installations, industrial activity, and high-energy technologies.
- Coal-related industries and infrastructure, including mining, logistics, terminals, stockpiles, and power generation facilities, are designated as essential industrial resources under section 303 of the Defense Production Act.
- Without presidential action, these capabilities cannot be supplied in a timely manner due to financial, regulatory, maintenance, and market challenges.
- The President authorizes purchases, commitments, and financial support to expand coal supply and power generation capacity as the most effective way to address these challenges.
- Requirements under sections 303(a)(1)-(a)(6) of the Act are waived to facilitate expansion efforts.
- The Secretary of Energy is directed to implement this determination and publish it in the Federal Register.

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity
WhiteHouse.summary: The White House issued a memorandum directing the Secretary of Energy regarding domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity. On January 20, 2025, President Trump declared a national energy emergency, stating that current U.S. energy production and infrastructure are insufficient and pose threats to the economy, national security, and foreign policy. The President determined that domestic petroleum resources and infrastructure are essential to national defense and that without federal intervention, the U.S. cannot quickly or adequately provide these resources due to financial, logistical, and regulatory challenges. He invoked section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 to authorize federal purchases, commitments, and financial support to expand petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity. He waived certain procedural requirements under the Act to facilitate this expansion promptly and directed the Secretary of Energy to implement these measures and publish the determination.

WhiteHouse.title: Presidential Determination Concerning the Air Force’s Jet Fighter Training Operations in Idaho, Oregon, and Nevada
WhiteHouse.summary: The President issued a memorandum exempting the U.S. Air Force’s jet fighter training operations in Idaho, Oregon, and Nevada from certain federal, state, interstate, and local water pollution control requirements, including administrative authority and sanctions. This exemption is granted under section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act and applies for one year, from April 20, 2026, to April 20, 2027. The exemption does not waive requirements under sections 1316 and 1317 of the Act. The memorandum clarifies that this exemption does not imply the Air Force would otherwise need permits for water pollution control, nor does it affect the enforcement of other laws applicable to these operations. The Secretary of the Air Force is directed to publish this determination in the Federal Register.
